evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jack jumps directly into 'Did you have any you know, main concerns or questions or anything like that' with no time-boxed framing or promise of a dependable quote, and no waiting for a yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as 'Did you have any you know, main concerns or questions or anything like that' — but this came before any discovery probing, so technically before probing, though the phrasing is weak and customer answered 'No, not at all' so no concerns were actually raised.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer stated no concerns, so nothing to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — customer raised no concerns, so no reflection was needed or possible.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Jack covered property type (1500 sq ft house), bedrooms (3), furniture breakdown (bed frames, living room, dining room items, garage items: rolling machine, punching bag), packing preference (customer packing), stops (none, straight move), and special considerations (washer/dryer, two computer desks, entertainment center as heaviest item). All seven items present.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Jack asked 'Were you guys gonna have everything boxed up and ready for us or did you need us to pack everything as well.' Customer declined, saying they would pack.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Jack stated 'Do you have a we typically would see maybe about fifty to seventy boxes in a house to your size. Does that sound reasonable or does that sound like overkill?' Customer confirmed reasonable.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jack gave a range: '3 to 4 hours loading, 45 minute drive, 2 to 3 hours unloading = 7 to 8 hour day' and personalized to this move: 'It does seem like it'll be probably a full truck. Relatively full house... nothing crazy nothing out of the ordinary.' Anchored with hourly rate ($202/hour for two movers) and travel fee ($150). Provided total estimate: '8 hours plus that travel fee you'd be looking at a total of $1,766.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Jack disclosed hourly rate ($101/person, $202 for two movers), what's included (wrapping, bed frame assembly/disassembly, TV mount removal), travel fee ($150), and explicitly stated no other costs: 'there's no additional costs there's no fuel charges, there's no credit card processing fees, there's no taxes there's no material charges. So there'll be no other surprise fees.' Did NOT mention 2.5-hour minimum or 15-minute-increment commitment framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Jack asked 'Do you have any questions about the pricing or, or the process, or anything like that' — not the 'Does that feel fair?' form called for, and did not wait for silence; customer immediately responded 'No, no, sounds good.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Jack moved directly to 'From here. What I can do is, I can you know, send you a quote or if you'd like, we'd love to help you out.' No closing of the Two Promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Jack never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final-concerns version. He went straight to quote/booking.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Jack never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Jack said 'if you'd like, we'd love to help you out. I can get you set up and scheduled now if you'd like' — but the customer circumvented this by requesting the quote be sent, and Jack agreed to send it first and said 'if you do want to move forward, all you gotta do is respond to that quote and say, let's book it.' Jack never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' plainly, and he provided an easy out (email the quote).
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Jack did not confirm the move at all. Customer asked for quote to be emailed, and Jack said he would send it and the customer would respond if ready. No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes were confirmed.

top_strength: Jack gathered comprehensive logistics details early and naturally — property size, bedroom breakdown, all furniture categories, appliances, and special items — which gave him solid data for a personalized estimate.
coaching_note: Jack skipped the foundational Section 1 time-boxed framing ('10–15 minutes, you walk away with a quote you can depend on'), never delivered either of the Two Promises, never asked the final concerns check or catch-all, and ended with no explicit ask or booking — he handed off to an email with no confirmation. Rebuild the structure: open with quid pro quo and wait for a yes, deliver both promises before closing, and ask for the business directly on the call.
